With a monotonic stack find, for every element, how far it extends left and right before a smaller value appears. That gives the longest window length where it is the minimum. Store the best such value for each length, then sweep lengths from n down to 1 taking the running maximum.

**Complexity:** O(n) time, O(n) space.

celebrity-problem.editorial:
## Approach

Keep a candidate. For each next person i, if the candidate knows i the candidate is out and i takes over. After the pass verify the candidate: everyone knows them and they know nobody.

**Complexity:** O(n) time, O(1) space.

integer-to-roman.editorial:
## Approach

Use the 13 Roman values in descending order, subtractive pairs included (900, 400, 90, 40, 9, 4). For each, append its symbol while it still fits into the number and subtract it.

**Complexity:** O(1) time, O(1) space.

kmp-pattern-search.editorial:
## Approach

Build the prefix function of the pattern. Scan the text keeping the length of the current match; on a mismatch fall back through the prefix function, on a full match record the start and fall back once more so overlaps are found.

**Complexity:** O(n + m) time, O(m) space.

minimum-characters-to-make-palindrome.editorial:
## Approach

The answer is n minus the length of the longest palindromic prefix. Compute it as the last value of the prefix function of s + '#' + reverse(s).

**Complexity:** O(n) time, O(n) space.

rat-in-a-maze-count.editorial:
## Approach

Depth-first search from the top-left. Mark the cell as visited, try the four moves into open unvisited cells and add up the paths that reach the goal, then unmark the cell (backtrack).

**Complexity:** O(4^(n^2)) worst case time, O(n^2) space.

binary-tree-preorder-traversal.editorial:
## Approach

Keep a stack. Pop a node, record it, push its right child and then its left child, so the left subtree is handled before the right.

**Complexity:** O(n) time, O(h) space.

binary-tree-postorder-traversal.editorial:
## Approach

Run an iterative traversal that records the node and then pushes left and right, which visits node, right, left. Reversing that order gives left, right, node.

**Complexity:** O(n) time, O(h) space.

left-view-of-binary-tree.editorial:
## Approach

Traverse level by level with a queue. The first node taken from the queue in each level is the one visible from the left.

**Complexity:** O(n) time, O(w) space.

top-view-of-binary-tree.editorial:
## Approach

BFS while tracking each node's horizontal distance (left -1, right +1). Store a value for a distance only the first time it is seen, then read the distances from smallest to largest.

**Complexity:** O(n log n) time, O(n) space.

bottom-view-of-binary-tree.editorial:
## Approach

BFS with horizontal distances. Overwrite the stored value for a distance every time a node arrives, so the last (lowest, and rightmost on ties) node stays. Read the distances in increasing order.

**Complexity:** O(n log n) time, O(n) space.

vertical-order-traversal-of-a-binary-tre.editorial:
## Approach

Walk the tree once and store (column, row, value) for every node. Sort the list, which orders columns left to right, rows top to bottom and values inside a cell. Start a new group whenever the column changes.

**Complexity:** O(n log n) time, O(n) space.

root-to-node-path-in-a-binary-tree.editorial:
## Approach

DFS with a path list: push the node, return true if it is the target or a child subtree finds it, otherwise pop it (backtrack) and return false.

**Complexity:** O(n) time, O(h) space.

maximum-width-of-binary-tree.editorial:
## Approach

BFS with an index per node. For each level the width is last index minus first index plus one. Re-basing the indices at the start of every level keeps them small.

**Complexity:** O(n) time, O(w) space.

boundary-traversal-of-binary-tree.editorial:
## Approach

Add the root, then the left boundary without leaves, then every leaf from left to right, then the right boundary without leaves in reverse order.

**Complexity:** O(n) time, O(h) space.

construct-binary-tree-from-inorder-and-p.editorial:
## Approach

Read postorder from the end: each value is a root. Find it in inorder with a hash map, build its right part first (the values after it) and then its left part.

**Complexity:** O(n) time, O(n) space.

flatten-binary-tree-to-linked-list.editorial:
## Approach

For each node with a left child, find the rightmost node of that left subtree, attach the node's right subtree to it, move the left subtree to the right and clear the left pointer. Then move on to the right child.

**Complexity:** O(n) time, O(1) space.

children-sum-property.editorial:
## Approach

Recursively check every node: a leaf passes, otherwise its value must equal the sum of its children (a missing child counts as 0) and both children must pass too.

**Complexity:** O(n) time, O(h) space.

fractional-knapsack.editorial:
## Approach

Sort items by value/weight (compare with cross-multiplication to avoid decimals). Take whole items while they fit, then the needed fraction of the next one. Scale by 100 using integer arithmetic.

**Complexity:** O(n log n) time, O(n) space.

minimum-number-of-coins.editorial:
## Approach

Go through the denominations from largest to smallest, take as many coins of each as fit into the remaining amount and continue with the remainder.

**Complexity:** O(1) time, O(1) space.

median-of-two-sorted-arrays.editorial:
## Approach

Binary search a cut in the shorter array; the cut in the longer one is implied. The cut is valid when both left maxima are at most both right minima. The median comes from those four values.

**Complexity:** O(log(min(m, n))) time, O(1) space.

merge-k-sorted-arrays.editorial:
## Approach

Put the first element of every array in a min-heap. Repeatedly pop the smallest, add it to the answer and push the next element of the same array.

**Complexity:** O(N log k) time, O(k) space.

k-maximum-sum-combinations.editorial:
## Approach

Sort descending. Start a max-heap with (0, 0). Each time you pop (i, j), push (i+1, j) and (i, j+1) if not seen before. After k pops you have the k largest sums.

**Complexity:** O(n log n + k log k) time, O(n + k) space.

next-greater-element.editorial:
## Approach

Go from right to left. Pop every stack value that is smaller than or equal to the current element; the top that remains is its next greater element. Then push the current value.

**Complexity:** O(n) time, O(n) space.

sort-a-stack.editorial:
## Approach

Recursively pop the top element, sort what is left, then insert the element back so larger values stay on top: pop smaller-than-it values, put it in, and push those values back.

**Complexity:** O(n^2) time, O(n) recursion space.

z-function.editorial:
## Approach

Maintain the rightmost window [l, r) that matches a prefix. For a new i inside it, start from min(r - i, z[i - l]) and extend by comparing characters. Each extension moves r forward, so the total is linear.

**Complexity:** O(n) time, O(n) space.

compare-version-numbers.editorial:
## Approach

Use two pointers. Parse the next dot-separated number from each version (0 when a version has ended) and compare. Return at the first difference, otherwise 0.

**Complexity:** O(n + m) time, O(1) space.
